title: Advent: John in the wilderness
hookLine: the second Sunday: prepare the way

cards: A man in a coat of camel's hair, a leather belt around his waist, stands in the river Jordan and shouts. He eats locusts and wild honey. He lives out in the wilderness.

And people come anyway, out of Jerusalem and the countryside, down to the water, confessing their sins and being baptized by him. He is not the one they've been waiting for, and he says so. He's the one clearing the road.
On the second Sunday of Advent, churches that keep the season light a second candle, and his voice comes back.

teach.b: Mark's Gospel opens with him, and with an old line from the prophets: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight." The picture is road-building.
Luke spells it out: "Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth".

teach.h: FILL THE VALLEYS, LEVEL THE HILLS.
teach.b: Before someone great arrives, you fill the potholes and take the boulders off the road. But clearing what?
The crowds asked John that question: "What shall we do then?" His answers are surprisingly ordinary.

teach.h: TWO COATS, HONEST BOOKS, FAIR HANDS.
teach.b: To everyone: "He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise." To the tax collectors: "Exact no more than that which is appointed you."
To the soldiers: "Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages." Notice what he doesn't say.
He doesn't tell the tax collectors to quit, or the soldiers to run off into the desert with him. Do your job, honestly. Share what you have.

That's the road. Christians differ on how John's call to repent is lived: some through confession to a priest before Christmas, some through quiet self-examination, some through a renewed promise at the altar.
Each points the way John did, away from himself. The road isn't for John. It's for the one coming after him.

how: In churches that keep Advent, the second Sunday's readings often tell of John the Baptist and his call to prepare the way of the Lord, and the second candle on the wreath is lit; some Christians make a confession or examine their lives before Christmas.

o: the season after Easter, leading to Pentecost
the days when the wise men's visit is kept
weeks of getting ready for Christ's coming

games.q: John at the river — tap the pairs.
p: let him impart to him that hath none
exact no more than is appointed

s: John tells the soldiers to leave the army
he tells them: "do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages."
Mark says John ate locusts and wild honey
and wore camel's hair with a leather belt.
in Luke, the crowd asks John: what shall we believe?
they ask: "what shall we do then?" and his answers are about coats, money and honest work.

games.q: you're a tax collector who walked out to the river to be baptized. you ask John: what shall we do? what does he tell you?
o: quit your job and follow me into the desert.
exact no more than that which is appointed you.
give everything you own to the temple.
games.why: Luke 3:13. not quit, but be honest. John's way is cleared by ordinary work done fairly.

practice: Ask the crowd's question of your own life, what shall I do then, and let one thing come up that's in the way: a grudge, a pile of unopened mail, a habit that keeps tripping someone you love, an extra coat in the closet.
Don't solve everything; just see that one thing clearly. If you pray, you can pray the line from Mark, prepare ye the way of the Lord; if you don't, hold the picture of an open road.

wordCard.voice: Advent. The weeks of waiting before Christmas. Its second Sunday brings John in the wilderness, crying prepare ye the way of the Lord.

orig.note: Greek: prepare ye the way of the Lord (Mark 1:3).

carryVoice: Your line: prepare the way. The road is for the one who's coming. See you tomorrow.
